head: 7b6532ad58cb0e00e167d720b226068dc98a3925
summary: I closed O-023 to O-029 and re-ran all three batches on real D:\ with the height now set before the scan. The hook sizes the window in a Loaded class handler, ahead of the window's own OnLoaded/StartScan, and refuses a window sized too late: 'scanning': false in all 35 re-run runs. Height-2 on the fixed primary metric is inconclusive (860 higher in 2 of 8 pairs, median 0.884, detectable 1.25x). The scan phase, reported and not decided on, shows 860 higher in 7 of 8 pairs (median 1.562). Trace-2 is render-path again (3 RENDER-PATH plus 1 SPLIT, no masking). Render-2 reads render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu by the rule, but with detectable 5.41x it rules nothing out, so the earlier gpu-present-side (render-1, flawed timing) is withdrawn. The findings record is rewritten around the second batches. The driver fixes are in: absolute -Out and trace/summary paths, exactly one valid line per run on both the live and -Reread paths, refusal of an -Out that already holds runs.jsonl, stripping of arm variables, and a reader that deletes stale stacks. StallStacks now matches its header and reads 10 ms traces, verified live (header 10,000,000 ns).

files.why: O-023: FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT is applied in a Loaded class handler (SizeOnLoad), before the window's own Loaded handler starts the scan. Sized() reports asked/height/workArea/scanning/ms/actual and refuses a window sized too late, a scan already started, or a height not applied.
O-024: FSA_T005_TRACE and FSA_T005_SUMMARY go through Path.GetFullPath against the current location, so a relative folder does not end up under the app's %TEMP% working directory.

O-024: absolute -Out. O-025: Resolve-Lines requires exactly one valid line per scheduled run on both the live and -Reread paths, and a live batch refuses an existing runs.jsonl. O-028: arm variables are stripped from each run's environment, and Test-RunLine stops the batch when traceFile disagrees with arm.trace. O-029: Invoke-StackReader deletes stacks-<n>.json first, and a failing reader becomes CANNOT-READ with its own text. Header updated.

O-026: header idle floor now says 25%, and the reason strings read 'no busy stretch covers 80% of the hook's wait'. O-027: the header documents the sample interval source and observedSampleMs is reported. R2-m5: an unparseable cached Speedscope file is removed and read as CANNOT-READ.
Expected reason follows the new wording.
O-027: NAMED timeline sampled every 10 ms.
O-027: the render-mixed timeline sampled every 10 ms.
O-025: -Reread with a missing run stops the batch.
O-025: -Reread with a doubled run stops the batch.
O-025: a line for a run not in the schedule stops the batch.
O-025: a live batch refuses an -Out with runs.jsonl, runs nothing and writes no verdict.
O-028: an untraced run that wrote a trace stops the batch.
O-028: a traced run with no trace stops the batch.
O-029: the real reader over a crashing StallStacks, with stale NAMED stacks left behind, gives CANNOT-READ, not the stale verdict.

O-023/O-026: corrected the height paragraph and the fallback trigger wording. Added a section on the superseded first batches, and rewrote the Height/Trace/Render findings, the reading of where each stall comes, and the fix candidate from height-2/trace-2/render-2.

obligations.how: TreeMode now sets FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT in a Loaded class handler registered as soon as the Application exists, the pattern size mode uses. It runs before MainWindow's own OnLoaded/StartScan, logs 'scanning' (whether ScanningPanel was up) and refuses a window sized too late or after the scan started. All 35 runs of height-2/trace-2/render-2 logged scanning:false, sized at 333-696 ms. I re-ran -Plan Height and -Plan Render as asked, and -Plan Trace too because its scan stretches were affected. T-003 still passes (4000 clamps to 1032 at 372 ms). The doc's height paragraph is corrected, a section declares that the first batches set the height after the scan started and are superseded, and the 'rescan's first move' reading is rewritten: the scan's first move now stalls 334-377 ms at 860 px.

T005Batch makes -Out absolute with GetFullPath($Out, (Get-Location).ProviderPath). New-T005Trace and the summary append resolve FSA_T005_TRACE and FSA_T005_SUMMARY the same way. Verified live twice. A hand-run T-005 with relative FSA_T005_TRACE/SUMMARY wrote artifacts/sl080/sample10/t005-1-34484.nettrace and found it. The Trace batch run with a relative -Out artifacts\sl080\trace-2 wrote all 4 traces into trace-2\traces and read them.

Invoke-Plan runs Resolve-Lines after the live batch and in place of it on -Reread: exactly one line per scheduled run, none outside the schedule, each passing Test-RunLine, else a stopped verdict and exit 1. A live batch refuses an -Out whose runs.jsonl exists. Fixtures reread-hole, reread-duplicate, reread-stray and live-existing-runs pass.

The StallStacks header now says 25% and documents the sample-interval source. Both reason strings, and the doc's fallback trigger list, now read 'no busy stretch covers 80% of the (hook's) wait'. The no-match fixture expects the new wording.

Recorded live: T-005 traced with FSA_T005_SAMPLE_MS=10 has a nettrace header SamplingNs of 10,000,000, and the UI thread's samples were seen 10.29 ms apart. StallStacks read that trace as RENDER-PATH with sampleMs 10. I added the fixtures named-10ms and render-mixed-10ms, which pass, and the reader now reports observedSampleMs beside the header's interval.

Invoke-T005Run removes every FSA_T005_*, FSA_HOOK_*, DOTNET_EventPipe*, DOTNET_EnableEventPipe and DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS key from the ProcessStartInfo environment before setting the arm's own. Test-RunLine stops the batch when traceFile disagrees with arm.trace; fixtures stop-trace-mismatch and stop-trace-missing pass. Live: all three re-run batches were started from a shell holding FSA_T005_TRACE, FSA_T005_SAMPLE_MS=5, FSA_T005_RENDER=software, FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT=700 and DOTNET_EventPipeConfig/OutputPath. All completed with no stop, no stray trace, and every hardware arm at renderMode Default.

The Trace reader is Invoke-StackReader. It deletes stacks-<n>.json before running StallStacks and returns CANNOT-READ with the reader's last output lines on a non-zero exit or no file. StallStacks also removes an unparseable cached Speedscope file and reads it as CANNOT-READ. Fixture trace-reader-crash (a throwing reader with stale NAMED stacks left behind) gives cannot-read, not NAMED.

deviations: Low arm 644 px, not 620 (unchanged from attempt 1): MinHeight has been 644 since SL-047, so 620 is refused by the hook, as measured live.
The sampling option is FSA_T005_SAMPLE_MS in hexadecimal ms, not FSA_T005_SAMPLE_NS (unchanged): measured, and now confirmed by the nettrace header (10,000,000 ns at 10 ms).
StallStacks idle floor 25% and time-first matching, busy for 80% of the wait (unchanged from attempt 1; the header text now says so, O-026).

O-028 strips FSA_HOOK_* and DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS too, beyond the FSA_T005_*/DOTNET_EventPipe* keys the finding named. An inherited FSA_HOOK_* would reach the app the same way, and WindowCases sets the hook's own for each launch.
I re-ran -Plan Trace as well as Height and Render, because the M1 disposition says trace-1's scan-phase stretches were affected by the same post-StartScan sizing.
not_built: FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG, the in-process fallback: contract only. Neither Trace batch reached cannot-read or tracing-masks.
A scan of the real contents of D:\ and any elevated ETW/WPR capture: both remain open questions for a person, as in attempt 1.
follow_ups: Run a Height batch with the scan phase's longest wait fixed as its figure before the runs. In height-2 it was 860 higher in 7 of 8 pairs (median 1.562), but that phase was not the pre-registered metric, so it is not a verdict.

Run a Render batch of 8 pairs. render-2's 4 pairs could only have detected a 5.41x difference, so whether the SyncFlush wait is GPU/present-side is unsettled; render-1's gpu-present-side was measured under the flawed timing.

The ~1.3 s later-move stall came in 6 of 17 runs of the superseded height-1, once in the second batches (render-2 run 8, software, 1,264 ms), and in a plain T-005 on C:\. It needs its own traced batch.
D:\fsa-sl080-temp is still in place from attempt 1; the engine blocked its removal. Every T-005 run removes its own case folder in it.
artifacts/sl080 holds superseded first batches (height-1, trace-1, render-1) beside the second ones. The doc marks them superseded; they are gitignored.

tests.note: 17 runs, no stop, no stray trace. Verdict inconclusive: 860 higher 2/8, median 0.884, logRatioSd 0.197, detectable 1.25, no order effect. Scan phase, not decided on: 860 higher 7/8, median 1.562.

tests.note: Verdict render-thread-or-dwm-not-gpu: software lower in 2 of 4 pairs, median 1.048, logRatioSd 0.812, detectable 5.41, so it rules nothing out. Software rescan was lower in 4 of 4 pairs (median 0.455), not decided on.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests\window\T005Batch.ps1 -Plan Height -Out artifacts\sl080\height-2 (first launch, from a shell that also held DOTNET_EnableEventPipe=1)
tests.note: My mistake: DOTNET_EnableEventPipe traced the launcher pwsh itself into the repo root (trace.nettrace). I stopped it during the warm-up, deleted the stray trace and the partial folder, and relaunched without that variable (the entry above).
With the height applied at load: 4000 clamps to 1032, sized at 372 ms, scanning:false. All opens under 500 ms.
